This Appeal under Section 14-A (2) of Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant-Deepak Pathak alias Umesh Kumar Pathak challenging the impugned order dated 07-12-2022 passed by the court of learned Special Judge/
S.T. / S.T. Act , Bahraich, in Bail Application No. 2753/12A of 2022, Deepak Pathak alias Umesh Kumar Pathak Vs. State of U.P. relating to Case Crime No. 529 of 2022, under Sections 354/316/
323/376-D I.P.C. & section 3(2)(V) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Police Station Khairighat, District Bahraich, whereby the bail application of the appellant has been rejected.
4. Prosecution story in brief is that mother-in-law of the prosecutrix lodged an first information report against the appellant stating there in that on 10-09-2022 at about 7:30 pm the accused persons started beating the informant's daughter-in-law and they even humiliated her.

sentences.text: Informant's daughter-in-law suffered injuries in the incident and the fetus developing in her womb died.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that neither in the first information report nor in her statement recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C., complainant has leveled allegation of rape against any accused person, only motive of old enmity has been told by her, which creates prosecution story doubtful.

It was further submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that there are material contradictions in the version of FIR and statement of prosecutrix recorded under section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and the statements of mother-in-law and husband of prosecutrix recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C.
6.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the allegation levelled against the appellant is nothing but an abuse of process of law and he is not involved in the aforesaid crime.
The entire allegation was made due to malafide intention whereas no such occurrence ever took place.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that co-accused Furtram having Anticipatory Bail Application no. 1721 of 2023 has already been granted anticipatory bail by co-ordinate bench of this court vide order dated 03-08-2023 and the case of the appellant is identical in nature and prays that appellant shall also be released on bail.

8. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submits that from perusal of version of F.I.R., statements of prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. and also from the perusal of medical report and the post mortem examination report of fetus, and further considering the long criminal antecedents of appellant, prima facie cognizanble offence is made out against the appellant.
The appellant is involved in heinous crime, thus he is not entitled to get any relief.

9. After considering the rival submissions as advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of record, this Court finds that in the first information report the prosecutrix, who is complainant, has made allegation against the appellant who is named in the F.I.R. thereafter, in the statements of prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. there is allegation agaisnt the appellant, nor she has made any contradictory statement, she has repeated the same version of the F.I.R. as well as her earlier statements recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., and perusal of Deepak Pathak Alias Umesh Kumar Pathak vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179740141/
2 medical report and the post mortem examination report of fetus, thus prima facie cognizable offence is made out against the appellant.

sentences.text: Coupled with the fact that co-accused Furtram was granted anticipatory bail on the ground that he was aged about 70 years of age and was not having any criminal history but the appellant is habitual offender and is having long criminal history of 7 cases including the present case as such he is not entitled to get any relief by this Court.
10. Thus, the impugned order dated 07-12-2022 does not want any interference by this Court.
11. In view of above, bail application of the appellant is rejected.
Consequently, the appeal is dismissed.

12. It is clarified that the observations, if any, made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of the prayer for bail and must not be construed to have any reflection on the ultimate merit of the case.
